analysis: 'Where' asks about a place. The answer often has a preposition like 'on', 'in' or 'under'.
exemplarContext: The cat is under the chair.

title: Time with 'at' and 'what time'
promptSentence: The class starts at nine.
targetTransformation: What time does the class start?
grammaticalCue: Ask 'What time' and use 'does'.
vietnamese: Hỏi giờ: 'What time' + do/does + chủ ngữ + động từ. Giờ cụ thể dùng 'at', ngày dùng 'on', tháng dùng 'in'. Tiếng Việt dùng 'lúc' cho tất cả.
formula: What time + do/does + subject + verb?
analysis: 'What time' asks about the clock. We use 'at' with a time in the answer.
exemplarContext: We have lunch at twelve.

title: Past Simple: Regular Verb
promptSentence: I walk to school every day.
targetTransformation: I walked to school yesterday.
grammaticalCue: Add -ed to the verb to talk about the past.
vietnamese: Thì quá khứ đơn với động từ có quy tắc: thêm -ed vào động từ. Tiếng Việt không đổi động từ mà dùng từ như "đã" hoặc "hôm qua".
formula: Subject + Verb-ed + Object
analysis: The verb 'walk' becomes 'walked'. We use the past simple for a finished action.
exemplarContext: She cleaned the kitchen last night.

title: Past Simple: Spelling of Regular Verbs
promptSentence: We study English and we plan a trip.
targetTransformation: We studied English and we planned a trip.
grammaticalCue: Change y to ied, and double the last letter in short verbs.
vietnamese: Quy tắc chính tả khi thêm -ed: study đổi thành studied, plan gấp đôi phụ âm thành planned. Tiếng Việt không có quy tắc này.
formula: consonant + y → ied; short verb: double the last consonant + ed
analysis: 'Study' ends in consonant plus y, so it becomes 'studied'. 'Plan' is a short verb, so we write 'planned'.
exemplarContext: He stopped the car and carried the bags.

title: Past Simple: Irregular Verb
promptSentence: I go to the market and buy some fruit.
targetTransformation: I went to the market and bought some fruit.
grammaticalCue: Use the special past form of irregular verbs.
vietnamese: Động từ bất quy tắc có dạng quá khứ riêng (go - went, buy - bought) và phải học thuộc. Tiếng Việt chỉ thêm "đã" nên không có dạng riêng này.
formula: Subject + Past Form (irregular) + Object
analysis: 'Go' becomes 'went' and 'buy' becomes 'bought'. These verbs do not take -ed.
exemplarContext: They ate rice and drank tea at lunch.

title: Past Simple: Negative
promptSentence: She visited her aunt on Sunday.
targetTransformation: She did not visit her aunt on Sunday.
grammaticalCue: Use did not and the base form of the verb.
vietnamese: Câu phủ định quá khứ: did not (didn't) + động từ nguyên mẫu. Động từ trở về dạng gốc, không còn -ed. Tiếng Việt dùng "không" hoặc "chưa".
formula: Subject + did not + Base Verb + Object
analysis: 'Did not' shows the past, so the main verb stays in the base form. We say 'did not visit', not 'did not visited'.
exemplarContext: I did not see my friends last weekend.

title: Past Simple: Yes/No Question
promptSentence: You watched a film last night.
targetTransformation: Did you watch a film last night?
grammaticalCue: Put did at the start and use the base form of the verb.
vietnamese: Câu hỏi Yes/No ở quá khứ: Did + chủ ngữ + động từ nguyên mẫu? Tiếng Việt thêm "không" hoặc "chưa" ở cuối câu, còn tiếng Anh đưa Did lên đầu.
formula: Did + Subject + Base Verb + Object?
analysis: 'Did' comes before the subject. The main verb goes back to the base form.
exemplarContext: Did he call you this morning?

title: Past Simple: Wh- Question
promptSentence: He bought a new phone yesterday.
targetTransformation: What did he buy yesterday?
grammaticalCue: Put the question word first, then did, the subject and the base verb.
vietnamese: Câu hỏi có từ để hỏi ở quá khứ: Wh-word + did + chủ ngữ + động từ nguyên mẫu? Trong tiếng Việt từ để hỏi ("cái gì") thường đứng cuối câu, còn tiếng Anh đưa lên đầu.
formula: Wh-word + did + Subject + Base Verb?
analysis: 'What' replaces 'a new phone' and goes to the front. 'Did' stays before the subject, so 'buy' is in the base form.
exemplarContext: Where did you go on holiday?

title: Past Continuous
promptSentence: I watch TV at eight o'clock.
targetTransformation: I was watching TV at eight o'clock last night.
grammaticalCue: Use was or were and the -ing form for an action in progress in the past.
vietnamese: Quá khứ tiếp diễn: was/were + V-ing, chỉ hành động đang diễn ra tại một thời điểm trong quá khứ. Tiếng Việt dùng "đang" kèm "lúc đó".
formula: Subject + was/were + Verb-ing
analysis: We use 'was' with I, he, she and it. We use 'were' with you, we and they.
exemplarContext: They were playing football at four o'clock.

title: Past Continuous with Past Simple
promptSentence: I cooked dinner. The phone rang.
targetTransformation: I was cooking dinner when the phone rang.
grammaticalCue: Use past continuous for the longer action and past simple for the short action.
vietnamese: Hành động dài đang diễn ra (was cooking) thì bị hành động ngắn chen vào (rang), nối bằng when. Giống cấu trúc "đang... thì..." trong tiếng Việt.
formula: Subject + was/were + Verb-ing + when + Subject + Past Simple
analysis: The long action is 'was cooking'. The short action is 'rang'.
exemplarContext: She was walking home when it started to rain.

title: Future with Going To: Plan
promptSentence: I visit my grandmother on Saturday.
targetTransformation: I am going to visit my grandmother on Saturday.
grammaticalCue: Use am, is or are + going to + base verb for a plan.
vietnamese: Dùng be going to + động từ nguyên mẫu cho dự định đã có từ trước. Tương đương "định" hoặc "sẽ" trong tiếng Việt.
formula: Subject + am/is/are + going to + Base Verb
analysis: The plan was made before now. The verb after 'to' is in the base form.
exemplarContext: We are going to have a picnic tomorrow.

title: Future with Going To: Negative
promptSentence: She is going to buy a new bag.
targetTransformation: She is not going to buy a new bag.
grammaticalCue: Put not after am, is or are.
vietnamese: Phủ định của be going to: thêm not sau am/is/are. Tiếng Việt dùng "không định" hoặc "sẽ không".
formula: Subject + am/is/are + not + going to + Base Verb
analysis: We keep 'going to' and add 'not' after 'is'. The main verb 'buy' does not change.
exemplarContext: They are not going to travel this summer.

title: Future with Going To: Question
promptSentence: You are going to cook tonight.
targetTransformation: Are you going to cook tonight?
grammaticalCue: Move am, is or are before the subject.
vietnamese: Câu hỏi với be going to: đảo am/is/are lên trước chủ ngữ. Tiếng Việt thêm "không" ở cuối câu hoặc dùng "có... không".
formula: Am/Is/Are + Subject + going to + Base Verb?
analysis: 'Are' moves to the front of the sentence. The rest of the sentence stays the same.
exemplarContext: Is she going to come to the party?

title: Future with Will: Decision or Offer
promptSentence: I open the window.
targetTransformation: I will open the window.
grammaticalCue: Use will + base verb for a quick decision or an offer.
vietnamese: Dùng will + động từ nguyên mẫu khi quyết định ngay lúc nói hoặc đưa ra lời đề nghị. Dịch là "sẽ" hoặc "để tôi".
formula: Subject + will + Base Verb
analysis: 'Will' does not change for any subject. The verb after 'will' is always in the base form.
exemplarContext: It is hot, so I will turn on the fan.

title: Future with Will: Negative
promptSentence: He will come to the meeting.
targetTransformation: He will not come to the meeting.
grammaticalCue: Put not after will. The short form is won't.
vietnamese: Phủ định với will: will not (won't) + động từ nguyên mẫu. Tiếng Việt dùng "sẽ không".
formula: Subject + will not (won't) + Base Verb
analysis: We add 'not' after 'will'. The short form 'won't' is common in speaking.
exemplarContext: I won't be late for class.

title: Future with Will: Question
promptSentence: It will rain tomorrow.
targetTransformation: Will it rain tomorrow?
grammaticalCue: Put will before the subject.
vietnamese: Câu hỏi với will: đưa will lên trước chủ ngữ. Tiếng Việt thêm "không" ở cuối: "Ngày mai trời sẽ mưa không?"
formula: Will + Subject + Base Verb?
analysis: 'Will' moves to the front. The main verb stays in the base form.
exemplarContext: Will you help me with my homework?

title: Present Continuous for Future Plans
promptSentence: I meet my friend at six.
targetTransformation: I am meeting my friend at six tonight.
grammaticalCue: Use am, is or are + verb-ing with a future time for a fixed plan.
vietnamese: Hiện tại tiếp diễn dùng cho kế hoạch đã sắp xếp trong tương lai gần, thường có từ chỉ thời gian như "tonight" hoặc "tomorrow". Tiếng Việt dùng "sẽ" hoặc "định".
formula: Subject + am/is/are + Verb-ing + future time
analysis: The word 'tonight' shows the future. The plan is fixed, for example with a time or a place.
exemplarContext: We are flying to Da Nang next week.

title: Present Continuous: Now vs Future Plan
promptSentence: He is cooking dinner now.
targetTransformation: He is cooking dinner with his friends tomorrow.
grammaticalCue: Change the time word from now to a future time.
vietnamese: Cùng một cấu trúc is cooking, nhưng now chỉ việc đang xảy ra, còn tomorrow chỉ kế hoạch tương lai. Thời gian trong câu quyết định nghĩa.
formula: Subject + am/is/are + Verb-ing + now (present) / tomorrow (future)
analysis: With 'now', the action is happening at this moment. With 'tomorrow', it is a plan for the future.
exemplarContext: I am studying now, and I am working on Monday.

title: Comparative: Short Adjective
promptSentence: My brother is tall. I am not very tall.
targetTransformation: My brother is taller than me.
grammaticalCue: Add -er to a short adjective and use than.
vietnamese: So sánh hơn với tính từ ngắn: adj-er + than. Tiếng Việt dùng "hơn": "cao hơn tôi".
formula: Subject + be + Adjective-er + than + Noun
analysis: 'Tall' becomes 'taller'. We use 'than' to compare two things.
exemplarContext: This bag is cheaper than that bag.

title: Comparative: Long Adjective
promptSentence: The train is fast. The bus is not fast.
targetTransformation: The train is more comfortable than the bus.
grammaticalCue: Use more before a long adjective, with no -er.
vietnamese: Với tính từ dài (từ hai âm tiết trở lên) dùng more + adj + than, không thêm -er. Tiếng Việt vẫn chỉ dùng "hơn".
formula: Subject + be + more + Adjective + than + Noun
analysis: 'Comfortable' is a long adjective, so we use 'more'. We never say 'more comfortabler'.
exemplarContext: English is more interesting than maths for me.

title: Comparative: Irregular and Spelling
promptSentence: Today is good and hot.
targetTransformation: Today is better, but yesterday was hotter.
grammaticalCue: Good becomes better, and short adjectives like hot double the last letter.
vietnamese: Một số tính từ đặc biệt: good - better, bad - worse. Tính từ ngắn như hot, big gấp đôi phụ âm cuối: hotter, bigger. Tiếng Việt không đổi hình thức từ.
formula: good → better; bad → worse; consonant + vowel + consonant → double + er
analysis: 'Good' has a special form, 'better'. 'Hot' becomes 'hotter' with a double t.
exemplarContext: My new phone is bigger and better than my old phone.

title: Superlative: Short Adjective
promptSentence: Mai is taller than her friends.
targetTransformation: Mai is the tallest girl in her class.
grammaticalCue: Use the + adjective-est for the number one in a group.
vietnamese: So sánh nhất với tính từ ngắn: the + adj-est + in/of + nhóm. Tiếng Việt dùng "nhất": "cao nhất lớp".
formula: Subject + be + the + Adjective-est + in/of + group
analysis: 'Tall' becomes 'the tallest'. We use 'in' with a place or a group, for example 'in her class'.
exemplarContext: This is the cheapest shop in town.

title: Superlative: Long Adjective
promptSentence: This film is more exciting than the other films.
targetTransformation: This is the most exciting film of all.
grammaticalCue: Use the most before a long adjective.
vietnamese: So sánh nhất với tính từ dài: the most + adj. Không nói "the excitingest". Tiếng Việt vẫn dùng "nhất".
formula: Subject + be + the most + Adjective + Noun
analysis: 'Exciting' is a long adjective, so we use 'the most'. We use 'of all' to mean 'compared with all the others'.
exemplarContext: She is the most helpful person in our team.

title: Modal Can: Ability
promptSentence: I swim.
targetTransformation: I can swim, but I cannot dance.
grammaticalCue: Use can or cannot + base verb for ability.
vietnamese: Can + động từ nguyên mẫu chỉ khả năng ("có thể", "biết"). Phủ định là cannot (can't). Can không thêm -s và không cần trợ động từ.
formula: Subject + can/cannot + Base Verb
analysis: 'Can' stays the same for every subject, so we say 'she can swim'. We make a question with 'Can you swim?'.
exemplarContext: He can cook rice, but he cannot cook fish.

title: Modal Should: Advice
promptSentence: You go to bed early.
targetTransformation: You should go to bed early.
grammaticalCue: Use should + base verb to give advice.
vietnamese: Should + động từ nguyên mẫu dùng để khuyên: "nên". Phủ định là should not (shouldn't) nghĩa là "không nên".
formula: Subject + should/shouldn't + Base Verb
analysis: 'Should' gives a friendly suggestion. It is not as strong as 'must'.
exemplarContext: You should drink more water when it is hot.

title: Modal Must and Have To: Rules
promptSentence: Students wear a uniform at school.
targetTransformation: Students must wear a uniform at school.
grammaticalCue: Use must or have to for a rule or something necessary.
vietnamese: Must và have to đều có nghĩa "phải". Must là quy định mạnh, have to là điều cần thiết từ bên ngoài. Phủ định khác nhau: mustn't là "cấm", don't have to là "không cần".
formula: Subject + must/have to + Base Verb
analysis: 'Must' is strong and does not change. With 'he' or 'she', we say 'has to'.
exemplarContext: She has to get up early on Monday.

title: Present Perfect: Result Now
promptSentence: I lost my keys, so I can't open the door.
targetTransformation: I have lost my keys, so I can't open the door.
grammaticalCue: Past action with a result that matters now uses have/has + past participle.
vietnamese: Hiện tại hoàn thành: hành động trong quá khứ nhưng kết quả còn ở hiện tại. Tiếng Việt dùng 'đã' cho mọi thì quá khứ, còn tiếng Anh phải chọn: 'have lost' (còn ảnh hưởng bây giờ) khác 'lost' (chỉ kể chuyện đã qua).
formula: Subject + have/has + Past Participle
analysis: The keys are still missing now, so the speaker uses the present perfect. The result is connected to the present.
exemplarContext: My sister has broken her phone, so she is using mine.

title: Present Perfect with 'for'
promptSentence: I started living here five years ago.
targetTransformation: I have lived here for five years.
grammaticalCue: 'For' + a length of time shows how long a situation has continued until now.
vietnamese: Dùng 'for' + khoảng thời gian (for five years = được năm năm). Tiếng Việt nói 'sống ở đây được năm năm' nên dễ dùng thì quá khứ; tiếng Anh dùng have + V3 vì việc vẫn tiếp diễn.
formula: Subject + have/has + Past Participle + for + period of time
analysis: The situation started in the past and continues now. 'For five years' tells us the length of time.
exemplarContext: They have known each other for ten years.

title: Present Perfect with 'since'
promptSentence: She began working at the bank in 2019.
targetTransformation: She has worked at the bank since 2019.
grammaticalCue: 'Since' + a starting point in time shows when a situation began.
vietnamese: Dùng 'since' + mốc thời gian (since 2019 = từ năm 2019). Khác với 'for' (khoảng thời gian), 'since' chỉ điểm bắt đầu. Tiếng Việt đều nói 'từ/được', nhưng tiếng Anh phải phân biệt hai từ này.
formula: Subject + have/has + Past Participle + since + starting point
analysis: The job began in 2019 and she still works there. 'Since' points to the start, not the length.
exemplarContext: We have lived in this town since last summer.

title: Present Perfect with 'just'
promptSentence: He arrived a minute ago.
targetTransformation: He has just arrived.
grammaticalCue: 'Just' between have/has and the participle means a very recent action.
vietnamese: 'Just' nghĩa là 'vừa mới'. Đặt giữa have/has và V3: 'has just arrived' (vừa mới đến). Tiếng Việt đặt 'vừa mới' trước động từ, tiếng Anh cũng đặt trước động từ chính nhưng sau trợ động từ.
formula: Subject + have/has + just + Past Participle
analysis: The action finished a very short time ago. 'Just' goes after has and before the participle.
exemplarContext: I have just finished my lunch, so I am not hungry.

title: Present Perfect with 'already'
promptSentence: I don't need to cook because my brother cooked dinner earlier.
targetTransformation: I don't need to cook because my brother has already cooked dinner.
grammaticalCue: 'Already' in a positive sentence shows something happened sooner than expected.
vietnamese: 'Already' nghĩa là 'đã... rồi' trong câu khẳng định, nhấn mạnh việc xong sớm hơn dự kiến. Đặt giữa have/has và V3. Tiếng Việt có 'đã... rồi' bao quanh động từ, tiếng Anh chỉ cần một từ 'already'.
formula: Subject + have/has + already + Past Participle
analysis: The dinner is ready now, so no cooking is needed. 'Already' stresses that it is done.
exemplarContext: We have already booked the hotel for our trip.

title: Present Perfect with 'yet'
promptSentence: Did you finish the report?
targetTransformation: Have you finished the report yet?
grammaticalCue: 'Yet' at the end of a question or negative sentence asks about something expected.
vietnamese: 'Yet' dùng trong câu hỏi và câu phủ định, nghĩa là 'chưa/đã... chưa', đặt ở cuối câu. Ví dụ: 'Have you finished yet?' (Bạn xong chưa?), 'I haven't finished yet' (Tôi chưa xong).
formula: Have/Has + Subject + Past Participle + yet?
analysis: The speaker expects the report to be done soon. 'Yet' goes at the end of the question.
exemplarContext: I haven't seen that film yet.

title: Present Perfect for Life Experience
promptSentence: This is my first time eating sushi.
targetTransformation: I have never eaten sushi before.
grammaticalCue: 'Never' with the present perfect talks about life experience up to now.
vietnamese: Dùng have/has + V3 với 'never/ever' để nói về kinh nghiệm sống ('chưa từng', 'đã từng'). Tiếng Việt dùng 'chưa từng/đã từng', tiếng Anh không nêu thời điểm cụ thể.
formula: Subject + have/has + never/ever + Past Participle
analysis: The sentence talks about all of the speaker's life until now. No exact time is given.
exemplarContext: Have you ever tried Vietnamese coffee with egg?

title: Present Perfect Continuous
promptSentence: I started waiting for the bus at six, and I am still waiting.
targetTransformation: I have been waiting for the bus since six.
grammaticalCue: Have/has been + verb-ing shows an action that began in the past and is still happening.
vietnamese: Hiện tại hoàn thành tiếp diễn nhấn mạnh hành động kéo dài liên tục đến bây giờ, như 'đang... mãi từ...'. Cấu trúc: have/has been + V-ing, thường đi với for/since.
formula: Subject + have/has + been + Verb-ing + for/since...
analysis: The waiting began at six and has not stopped. The continuous form shows the action is still in progress.
exemplarContext: It has been raining for two hours.

title: Zero Conditional: Facts
promptSentence: Water boils when you heat it to 100 degrees.
targetTransformation: If you heat water to 100 degrees, it boils.
grammaticalCue: Zero conditional uses present simple in both clauses for facts that are always true.
vietnamese: Câu điều kiện loại 0 nói về sự thật hiển nhiên: If + hiện tại đơn, hiện tại đơn. Tiếng Việt dùng 'nếu... thì...' và không đổi thì; tiếng Anh cũng giữ hiện tại đơn ở cả hai vế.
formula: If + Present Simple, Present Simple
analysis: This is always true, so both verbs are in the present simple. 'If' can be replaced by 'when'.
exemplarContext: If you mix red and blue, you get purple.

title: Zero Conditional: Habits and Rules
promptSentence: Plants die when they don't get water.
targetTransformation: If plants don't get water, they die.
grammaticalCue: Zero conditional can also describe a general rule or a result that always follows.
vietnamese: Câu điều kiện loại 0 cũng dùng cho quy luật chung. Cả hai vế dùng hiện tại đơn, không dùng 'will'. Sai thường gặp: 'If plants don't get water, they will die' khi nói quy luật chung.
formula: If + Subject + Present Simple, Subject + Present Simple
analysis: The rule is general, so we do not use 'will'. The if-clause can also come second without a comma.
exemplarContext: If I drink coffee late at night, I can't sleep.

title: First Conditional: Warning
promptSentence: Study hard or you will fail the test.
targetTransformation: If you don't study hard, you will fail the test.
grammaticalCue: First conditional uses if + present simple, then will + base verb, for a real future result.
vietnamese: Câu điều kiện loại 1 nói về khả năng có thật ở tương lai: If + hiện tại đơn, will + động từ nguyên mẫu. Tiếng Việt dùng thì hiện tại cho cả hai vế, nhưng tiếng Anh không dùng 'will' sau 'if'.
formula: If + Present Simple, will + Base Verb
analysis: The if-clause uses the present simple, not 'will'. The main clause uses 'will' for the future result.
exemplarContext: If you leave now, you will arrive on time.

title: First Conditional: Plans
promptSentence: It might rain tomorrow, so we may stay at home.
targetTransformation: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home.
grammaticalCue: Use if + present simple for a possible future event and will for the plan.
vietnamese: Dùng 'if + hiện tại đơn' cho sự kiện có thể xảy ra ngày mai, và 'will' cho kết quả. 'If it rains' (không phải 'if it will rain') dịch là 'nếu ngày mai trời mưa'.
formula: If + Subject + Present Simple, Subject + will + Base Verb
analysis: Rain tomorrow is possible, not certain. The if-clause stays in the present simple even though it is about the future.
exemplarContext: If I have time on Saturday, I will visit my grandparents.

title: Second Conditional
promptSentence: I don't have a lot of money, so I can't buy a new car.
targetTransformation: If I had a lot of money, I would buy a new car.
grammaticalCue: Second conditional uses if + past simple and would + base verb for unreal or unlikely situations.
vietnamese: Câu điều kiện loại 2 nói về điều không có thật ở hiện tại: If + quá khứ đơn, would + động từ nguyên mẫu. Quá khứ đơn ở đây không chỉ quá khứ, mà chỉ sự giả định. Tiếng Việt dùng 'nếu... thì...' không đổi thì.
formula: If + Past Simple, would + Base Verb
analysis: The speaker does not have much money now, so the situation is imaginary. The past form 'had' shows it is not real.
exemplarContext: If I lived closer to the city, I would go there more often.

title: Wish + Past Simple
promptSentence: I don't live near the sea, and I'm sad about it.
targetTransformation: I wish I lived near the sea.
grammaticalCue: 'Wish' + past simple expresses a wish about a present situation that is not true.
vietnamese: 'Wish' + quá khứ đơn diễn tả điều ước trái với thực tế hiện tại ('ước gì'). Tiếng Việt chỉ nói 'ước gì tôi sống gần biển', còn tiếng Anh phải lùi một thì: 'lived', không phải 'live'.
formula: Subject + wish + Subject + Past Simple
analysis: The speaker does not live near the sea now. The past simple shows the wish is not real.
exemplarContext: I wish I had more free time.

title: 'Unless' in Conditionals
promptSentence: If you don't hurry, you will miss the train.
targetTransformation: Unless you hurry, you will miss the train.
grammaticalCue: 'Unless' means 'if not' and is followed by a positive verb.
vietnamese: 'Unless' nghĩa là 'trừ khi / nếu không', đã mang nghĩa phủ định nên động từ phía sau ở dạng khẳng định. Tiếng Việt dùng 'nếu không', nên người học hay viết sai 'unless you don't hurry'.
formula: Unless + Subject + Positive Verb, Subject + will + Base Verb
analysis: 'Unless you hurry' has the same meaning as 'if you do not hurry'. We do not add 'not' after 'unless'.
exemplarContext: Unless it rains, we will have the picnic in the park.

title: Time Clauses with Future Meaning
promptSentence: First I will finish my homework. Then I will watch TV.
targetTransformation: I will watch TV after I finish my homework.
grammaticalCue: After a time word like 'after', 'when' or 'before', we use the present simple for the future.
vietnamese: Sau 'when, after, before, as soon as' dùng hiện tại đơn dù nghĩa là tương lai. Tiếng Việt nói 'sau khi tôi làm xong bài tập' không đổi thì, nhưng tiếng Anh không dùng 'will' trong mệnh đề thời gian.
formula: Main clause (will + Base Verb) + after/when/before + Present Simple
analysis: The homework comes first, then the TV. The time clause uses the present simple, not 'will finish'.
exemplarContext: I will call you when I get home.

title: Present Passive
promptSentence: People speak English in many countries.
targetTransformation: English is spoken in many countries.
grammaticalCue: Present passive uses am/is/are + past participle when the action is more important than the doer.
vietnamese: Câu bị động hiện tại: am/is/are + V3. Dùng khi người làm không quan trọng. Tiếng Việt dùng 'được/bị' ('Tiếng Anh được nói ở nhiều nước'); tiếng Anh dùng to be + V3.
formula: Object + am/is/are + Past Participle
analysis: The object of the active sentence becomes the subject. We do not need to say who speaks English.
exemplarContext: Rice is grown in many parts of Vietnam.

title: Past Passive
promptSentence: Someone stole my bike last night.
targetTransformation: My bike was stolen last night.
grammaticalCue: Past passive uses was/were + past participle.
vietnamese: Câu bị động quá khứ: was/were + V3. Tiếng Việt thường thêm 'bị' cho việc không hay ('xe bị lấy cắp') hoặc 'được' cho việc tốt; tiếng Anh dùng cấu trúc giống nhau cho cả hai.
formula: Object + was/were + Past Participle
analysis: We do not know who took the bike, so the passive is natural. The bike is the subject now.
exemplarContext: This house was built in 1990.

title: Present Perfect Passive
promptSentence: They have built a new bridge in our town.
targetTransformation: A new bridge has been built in our town.
grammaticalCue: Present perfect passive uses have/has + been + past participle.
vietnamese: Bị động hiện tại hoàn thành: have/has + been + V3. Tiếng Việt nói 'Một cây cầu mới đã được xây'; tiếng Anh phải có 'been' giữa 'has' và V3.
formula: Object + have/has + been + Past Participle
analysis: The bridge now exists, so we use the present perfect. 'Been' is needed in the passive form.
exemplarContext: Many new shops have been opened in the city centre.

title: Reported Statements
promptSentence: He said, "I am tired."
targetTransformation: He said (that) he was tired.
grammaticalCue: In reported speech, the verb usually moves one tense back and the pronouns change.
vietnamese: Câu tường thuật: lùi một thì (am -> was) và đổi đại từ (I -> he). Tiếng Việt chỉ thêm 'rằng' ('anh ấy nói rằng anh ấy mệt') mà không đổi thì, nhưng tiếng Anh phải lùi thì.
formula: Subject + said (that) + Subject + Past Form
analysis: The present 'am' changes to the past 'was'. 'I' changes to 'he' because we are talking about him.
exemplarContext: Anna said that she liked my new haircut.

title: Reported Wh-Questions
promptSentence: He asked, "Where do you live?"
targetTransformation: He asked me where I lived.
grammaticalCue: In reported questions, the word order is like a statement and there is no 'do/does'.
vietnamese: Câu hỏi tường thuật với từ để hỏi: dùng trật tự câu khẳng định, bỏ do/does và lùi thì ('do you live' -> 'I lived'). Không dùng dấu chấm hỏi. Tiếng Việt giữ nguyên trật tự nên người học hay viết 'where did I live'.
formula: asked + (object) + wh-word + Subject + Past Verb
analysis: The question word stays at the front. The subject comes before the verb, as in a statement.
exemplarContext: She asked me what time the film started.

title: Reported Yes/No Questions
promptSentence: She asked, "Do you like coffee?"
targetTransformation: She asked me if I liked coffee.
grammaticalCue: Reported yes/no questions use 'if' or 'whether' and statement word order.
vietnamese: Câu hỏi Yes/No tường thuật: dùng 'if' hoặc 'whether' (liệu/có... không), trật tự khẳng định, lùi thì. Tiếng Việt dùng 'có... không' ('cô ấy hỏi tôi có thích cà phê không'), còn tiếng Anh cần 'if'.
formula: asked + (object) + if/whether + Subject + Past Verb
analysis: The direct question 'Do you like...' becomes 'if I liked...'. We do not use 'do' in the reported question.
exemplarContext: He asked me if I had finished my homework.

title: Relative Clause with 'who'
promptSentence: I met a girl. She plays the violin.
targetTransformation: I met a girl who plays the violin.
grammaticalCue: 'Who' joins two sentences and refers to a person.
vietnamese: 'Who' là đại từ quan hệ chỉ người, thay cho 'she/he/they'. Tiếng Việt dùng 'mà/người mà' ('cô gái mà chơi violin'); tiếng Anh dùng 'who' ngay sau danh từ chỉ người.
formula: Noun (person) + who + Verb...
analysis: 'Who' replaces 'she' and joins the two sentences. It comes straight after 'a girl'.
exemplarContext: The man who lives next door is a doctor.

title: Relative Clause with 'which' and 'that'
promptSentence: This is the book. I bought it yesterday.
targetTransformation: This is the book that I bought yesterday.
grammaticalCue: 'Which' or 'that' joins two sentences and refers to a thing.
vietnamese: 'Which/that' là đại từ quan hệ chỉ vật. Tiếng Việt dùng 'mà' ('quyển sách mà tôi mua hôm qua'). Khi 'that' là tân ngữ, có thể bỏ: 'the book I bought yesterday'.
formula: Noun (thing) + which/that + Subject + Verb...
analysis: 'That' replaces 'it' and joins the two sentences. We do not repeat 'it' after the verb.
exemplarContext: The phone which I use every day is very old.
